messages:
alex kim: Heads-up, intake backlog keeps growing because both teams run fullbench. Proposal: split ownership. Infra owns ingress/runtime safety smokes; ML owns deep quality bench and golden artifacts.

maya singh: Agreed. Can we define the minimal manifest fields infra needs to run deterministic smokes? Tokenizer id, tokenizer_hash, seqlen, artifact_sha, eval_set, repro_seed, thresholds.

sergey petrov: From infra: we also need a cheap ensemble smoke (fp16 + int8 shadow) on a small sample to catch quantization regressions. Keep job under ~10 minutes.

nina r.: Also document ACLs/KMS in the manifest so infra can fetch artifacts without manual ACLs. Private models need allowed_orgs and kms_key_id.

jordan: Thinking runtime signal: expose a compact "compat_score" header (0..100) plus categorical perf_risk (low/med/high). Rollout-service can map these to policies.

ops-liz: We'll wire rollback on perf_risk or compat_score drops. Need a single signal to subscribe to; recommend compat_score + error_rate.

alex kim: Action items: maya+nina draft manifest schema (Weds), sergey+infra build ensemble-smoke prototype (500 samples) next Tue, jordan+ops hook compat headers into rollout by EOW. I'll write an RFC after meeting.

maya singh: I'll open a short PR for manifest proto and include thresholds list so automation can apply ML thresholds.

sergey petrov: Prototype plan: run int8 shadow on 500 golden prompts, compute token edit distance + p95 latency, emit compat metrics. Keep it cheap to iterate.

nina r.: Add PII/KMS checklist to schema. No public artifacts without explicit allowed_orgs.

jordan: I'll make rollout tickets and a tiny sequence diagram for compat flow.

alex kim: Thanks. If no objections, we'll proceed with the split and the staged acceptance flow: fast smoke -> sampled bench -> canary -> fullbench pre-GA. End.
